speaker: narrator
text: Act IV: The Final Confrontation

speaker: narrator
text: With the Lifelight Elixir in hand, you stand before Malakar's fortress. The obsidian gates loom ahead, wreathed in shadow and ancient magic. Mira steps through the gates beside you, pale but unbending. She and Sir Cedric take up their places just inside the threshold — someone must hold the way out. A small light settles on the gatepost: Nyx, keeping close.

speaker: mira
text: Someone has to keep the way out open, and that's me. So come back through it.

speaker: sir cedric
text: I held a gate once and lost a king behind it. I will not lose this one, or you.

speaker: nyx
text: I'll be the light at the edge of your eye. Don't look for me. Just know.

speaker: narrator
text: Mira presses something into your hand: a small silver medallion, two hands clasped on its face. Sir Cedric lays his hand over hers; the light on the gatepost leans in.

speaker: mira
text: If it goes quiet in there, say our names. We'll hear.

speaker: narrator
text: The halls beyond are yours to walk, but you will not be far from them.

speaker: narrator
text: Towering obsidian gates loom before you, carved with writhing shadows that seem to move in the corners of your vision. Three ancient ward stones, left, middle and right, pulse with malevolent energy, casting eerie purple light across the threshold. The air crackles with dark magic, and whispers of forgotten souls echo from beyond the barrier. Spectral guardians drift between the stones, their hollow eyes fixed upon any who dare approach this cursed entrance.

speaker: narrator
text: Malakar's fortress stands before you, and somewhere inside King Alden is held captive. Break through its defences and face the sorcerer.

speaker: narrator
text: Shadow guardians and a barrier of dark energy bar the way into the fortress. Find what feeds them, and break their hold on the gates.

speaker: narrator
text: Elior's light breaks the guardians' hold on the gates. The ward stones fall dark, and the way into Malakar's fortress lies open.

speaker: narrator
text: You take the Guardian's Chain. As you lift the Guardian's Chain, you feel a surge of protective energy coursing through your body. The chain's light grows brighter, recognizing you as its new bearer.

speaker: narrator
text: Malakar's servants wander the courtyard in chains of shadow, bound to serve him against their will. Win their trust, and break the chains.

speaker: narrator
text: This was a garden once. The fountains still stand under a sky that never quite rains, but what runs down them is black and slow, and the statues have all turned their faces away. Grey figures walk the paths in circles, chains of shadow at their ankles, never looking up. By the dry fountain a soldier in a soot-black royal tabard stands rigid, staring at nothing.

speaker: narrator
text: The Trapped Servants watch you from the corners of their eyes and keep walking. One whispers, without stopping:

speaker: trapped servants
text: 'Others came through that gate. They were all brave, until the guardians. If you were braver than the guardians, you would carry something of theirs.'

speaker: narrator
text: The Captain of the Guard stares through you.

speaker: captain of the guard
text: 'I held the gate for King Alden once. Now I hold it for... I cannot remember.'

speaker: narrator
text: The Trapped Servants have stopped walking. They stand close together, watching you.

speaker: trapped servants
text: 'We are so tired. Whatever you can do for us, do it gently.'

speaker: narrator
text: Elior's courage earns the servants' trust, and a blessing breaks their chains. Freed, they offer what help they can for the trials ahead.

speaker: narrator
text: The Freed Servants bow. One of them, an old woman with flour still in the creases of her hands, looks up.

speaker: freed servants
text: 'I was the king's cook. I do not know how long ago.'

speaker: narrator
text: The Captain of the Guard lifts his head and meets your eyes.

speaker: captain of the guard
text: 'I remember now. King Alden used to walk the walls at night and talk to whoever was on them. That is how they got him. Cedric stood his post — it was shadows that came for Alden, not any blade of ours. If you see Sir Cedric again, tell him I am sorry I ever doubted him.'

speaker: captain of the guard
text: 'They tell me the gates are open. I would walk out of them tonight, if my hand remembered the sword. Every shadow between here and home knows my face.'

speaker: narrator
text: Countless mirrors show false paths and twisted reflections. Find the one true way through the labyrinth.

speaker: narrator
text: Corridors of mirror run away from you in impossible directions, and in every one of them a different Elior looks back. You stand at the mouth of the maze, facing north.

speaker: narrator
text: A knight in a grey cloak bars the stair to the Tower of Shadows, lost in a despair no blade can reach. Learn the truth of him, and find a way past.

speaker: narrator
text: A long hall of old banners, so high the ceiling is lost. Everything that was ever said here is still being said, very quietly: orders, jokes, names, someone counting. Tattered banners hang high along the walls, grimed past reading. At the far end, before the stair, a knight in tarnished armour stands without moving, the way a man stands at a grave. Sir Cedric has followed you in; he stands by the south door, his eyes on the knight.

speaker: an echo
text: 'Left, then left, then the way your shadow does not go.'

speaker: knight of despair
text: There is nothing you can say to me that I have not already told myself. Go. Return when you have the truth.

speaker: sir cedric
text: That voice. I have heard it before, Elior, I would swear to it. I cannot see the face that goes with it.

speaker: narrator
text: You take the Echo Stone. You lift a smooth grey stone from a niche beneath the banners. It is warm, and when you hold it to your ear you hear the hall's echoes still speaking inside it.

speaker: narrator
text: Your reflection still walks the north corridor. The east corridor stays empty.

speaker: narrator
text: Guided by the servants' pendant and the hall's echoes, Elior walks the one true path through the mirrors, and learns to see through illusion.

speaker: narrator
text: The true path is already clear. The false mirrors stay dark.

speaker: true self
text: You told Mira you came for the king. Tell me why you really came.

speaker: knight of despair
text: So you see something of me. That is not the same as knowing me. Look around you, if you must know.

speaker: sir cedric
text: Grey cloak, twisted rune. I know him now. Do what you came to do. I will hear what he has to say.

speaker: knight of despair
text: So you see me. Then you know what I am, and what I have done. There is no redemption for a man like me. Do not waste the word.

speaker: narrator
text: The chain is already lit. His sorrow does not reach you.

speaker: sir cedric
text: You.

speaker: knight of despair
text: Me.

speaker: knight of despair
text: I was the stranger in Willowbrook. Malakar sent me for an amulet, and for the child it hid. It was my token that fouled your well.

speaker: knight of despair
text: The night King Alden was taken, I paid the watch to look away. The captain of the watch was a good man. I made sure he was asleep. And I put my seal to the lie that shamed Sir Cedric.

speaker: knight of despair
text: And when I saw what my master was doing to the king, I stopped believing he could be saved. That is all despair is. You have given me something to believe in again.

speaker: knight of despair
text: Sir Cedric. I am sorry. I have no right to ask anything of you, so I will not.

speaker: sir cedric
text: I heard you. That will have to be enough, for now.

speaker: narrator
text: Elior sees the knight as he truly is and offers him redemption instead of a blade. The man who framed Sir Cedric confesses, and the stair to the Tower of Shadows lies open.

speaker: redeemed knight
text: I will wait here. If you come back down those stairs, I will know there is still hope.

speaker: sir cedric
text: Go on up. I will keep an eye on him.

speaker: narrator
text: The warriors do not hear you. They are still fighting.

speaker: narrator
text: A stair winds up inside the black stone, narrow and dark. The walls are cold, and there are no windows. The shadows on the stair move a moment after you do. With every step, something quiet at your ear tells you why you should not have come.

speaker: mira
text: I'm at the gate, Elior. I said I'd hold it, and I'm holding it.

speaker: sir cedric
text: A knight does not leave his post. Mine is the threshold. Go on, lad.

speaker: nyx
text: Left? I'm right here. I never was anywhere else.

speaker: narrator
text: The whispers have nothing left to say. They thin like smoke, and the stair above lies open.

speaker: narrator
text: The token is quiet and warm. The whispers are gone.

speaker: narrator
text: At the top of the tower the Sorceress of Lies holds court, and the mask on her staff is the mark that lay beneath Elena's curse. See through her lies, and find what lies beneath them.

speaker: narrator
text: A round room at the top of the tower, and the only beautiful room in the fortress. That is what is wrong with it. Crystals grow from the walls, each humming something kind and untrue, and the floor gives a little under your feet, like ice that might hold. At the chamber's heart the Sorceress of Lies waits, her staff crowned with a small silver mask. Your breath catches: it is the mask from Elena's wrist.

speaker: narrator
text: The token is still warm against your heart. Her whispers cannot reach you.

speaker: sorceress of lies
text: Little Elior. Your parents sold you to save themselves, did you know? Malakar told me so himself. Turn back.

speaker: narrator
text: She has seen the badge. She cannot stop looking at it.

speaker: sorceress of lies
text: He turned? Then he is a fool. Everyone lies, little Elior. No one has ever understood a word I said. Why would you be the first?

speaker: sorceress of lies
text: Elena. The girl at the inn. Malakar wanted every healer in the kingdom at her bedside and none at the king's. So I cursed her, and set my mask on her wrist so they would know whose work it was, and fear it. And I watched the inn door, to see who would come for a mark like that. The healer from Willowbrook never did. I should have known then what that meant.

speaker: sorceress of lies
text: I told the king's physicians he was only tired. I told the court he had gone hunting. I have told so many lies that I forgot what my own voice sounds like. And I told you your parents sold you. Mine did. I wanted it to be true of everyone, so that it would not only be true of me.

speaker: sorceress of lies
text: No one has ever spoken to me without a lie. Not Malakar, not his servants, not the ones I cursed. You are the first. I did not know it would hurt.

speaker: narrator
text: Elior sees through the Sorceress's lies and answers the loneliness beneath them. She confesses the curse on Elena, and the arch to the north opens.

speaker: unmasked sorceress
text: Go on, through the arch. What waits there has been waiting for you longer than I have. And Elior — tell Elena I am sorry. It is the first true thing I have asked anyone to carry.

speaker: narrator
text: Among the broken memories a shadow reaches for scenes it cannot hold. Mend what it has lost, and learn whose voice it is.

speaker: narrator
text: This mystical chamber exists partially outside of time itself, its walls covered in floating orbs of crystallized memory that flicker with scenes from long ago. The air ripples with temporal distortions, and fragments of the past drift like spectral snow through the space. At the room's center, a shadowy figure wavers between existence and void, reaching out with desperate longing toward memories that seem to slip away like morning mist.

speaker: shadow of the past
text: Elior. You came.

speaker: narrator
text: The shadow's lips move, but the vault swallows the sound.

speaker: narrator
text: The orbs are whole. The stone lies quiet in your hand.

speaker: shadow of the past
text: She lied for him for years, and still she chose the truth. Then perhaps he can too. But not by force, Elior. Never by force.

speaker: shadow of the past
text: I was Malakar, once. Not the one who waits in the throne room: the part of him that remembered why he began. When he tore the wound, he tore himself in two, and I am the half he left behind. I held you once, when you were small enough to fit in my two hands. I have called to you ever since.

speaker: shadow of the past
text: Every time, with the same words, and you caught only pieces of them. Hear them whole: be patient where I was not. Close what I opened, and let them rest.

speaker: narrator
text: The Shadow has seen the mask. It is enough.

speaker: shadow of the past
text: The Phoenix asked us once what wisdom is when time is short. Aren and Lysa knew. I did not.

speaker: shadow of the past
text: Patience. The one thing I never had. Then I will wait, a little longer. Take the amulet east, Elior. It will open for you.

speaker: narrator
text: Elior learns that the voice from his dreams is what remains of Malakar's better self. The sealed door to the east now answers to the amulet.

speaker: shadow of the past
text: Go east, Elior. I have seen those memories every day for years. You never have.

speaker: narrator
text: Behind the sealed door, Aren and Lysa's last memories wait. Look into them, and learn the whole truth before the throne room.

speaker: narrator
text: A small, quiet room. Nothing here is threatening. Memories hang in the air like lanterns, warm and still, and every one of them has your parents in it. It is the saddest and warmest room in the fortress.

speaker: lysa
text: Hold it shut, Aren. Hide him. That is enough.

speaker: narrator
text: Elior sees the whole truth: his parents' friendship with Malakar, the wound, and the ward they became. The way north to the Throne Chamber opens.

speaker: narrator
text: The lanterns are dim now. You do not need to look again; you will not forget.

speaker: narrator
text: A vast chamber under a broken dome. A throne of black stone, twisted like a root, stands at its head. Above a ritual circle King Alden hangs in a prison of crystal, and from his crown a thin thread of light bleeds into a rift in the air: the wound in time. Malakar stands beside it, grey and failing. The wound is killing him too.

speaker: shadow of the past
text: Not like this.

speaker: malakar
text: You would waste it on me? You have not even heard what I am offering.

speaker: malakar
text: Aren's son. You have their eyes, both of them. You have seen the vault, so you know what I did, and you know it worked. They woke, Elior. For a little while, they woke.

speaker: malakar
text: The wound runs backwards. Open it all the way and it pulls the days back to before the fever, and they wake at the workbench as they were. I am not lying to you. I have done the sums.

speaker: malakar
text: Only the ward holds it shut: half in your amulet, half in Alden's crown. I have been bleeding the king for years to loosen his half. Give me yours and he can stop dying today.

speaker: malakar
text: And the price is the rest of it. The king. Every year the kingdom has had since. And you. You were born after the tear, Elior. When the days go back, you go with them. I am sorry. The sums are still right.

speaker: narrator
text: King Alden sleeps in the crystal and does not hear you.

speaker: malakar
text: You would waste it on me? Keep it for them, then. Give me the amulet, Elior, and your mother wakes before that glass is empty.

speaker: malakar
text: They would wake, Elior. Your mother would laugh at something your father said. Is one boy and one tired king too much to pay for that? Give me the amulet.

speaker: malakar
text: We carved those words together, your father and I. I had forgotten them.

speaker: shadow of the past
text: Elior. I tore the world to keep them, and I lost them anyway. I could not wait; you can. Be patient where I was not. Close what I opened, and let them rest.

speaker: malakar
text: Then show me what they left you.

speaker: narrator
text: “You tore the world, Malakar,” you say. “You drained the king. You sent a man to hunt a child in Willowbrook, and you let Sir Cedric take the blame. I will not pretend you didn't.”

speaker: malakar
text: No. You won't. Your mother never could either.

speaker: narrator
text: The open amulet grows heavy in your hand, ready.

speaker: narrator
text: You press the open amulet to the wound. Threads of gold rise from King Alden's crown and weave into the ward's light. The tear closes, and Malakar goes with it, drawn into the seal. He does not fight.

speaker: malakar
text: I am sorry. Tell them— no. They know.

speaker: narrator
text: The last of him to go is his voice, low: "…the field will wake." Then the seal is shut.

speaker: king alden
text: Then it falls to me to set right what he broke. Rest now. You have done enough.

speaker: narrator
text: Where the wound was, the light of the amulet gathers into two shapes you have only ever seen in the vault's memories: a man with your eyes, and a woman with Grandmother's smile. Your parents.

speaker: aren
text: Elior. Look at you. Taller than me, I think.

speaker: lysa
text: We watched over you all this time, from inside the light. We could not hold you, but we could hold the door shut.

speaker: aren
text: You named what he did, and you did not hate him for it. That is the hardest kind of fair.

speaker: aren
text: The ward is finished, and so are we. Tell your grandmother we are proud of her. Tell her we are resting.

speaker: lysa
text: Go home, love. The field is waiting.

speaker: narrator
text: The light thins. They smile, and they are gone. The amulet in your hand is only a locket now, warm and quiet. Your parents are at rest.

speaker: narrator
text: Behind the throne an arch you had not noticed stands open. Beyond it, far off, the road runs home.

speaker: narrator
text: You have completed the quest 'The Final Stand'.

speaker: king alden
text: Go home, Elior. The kingdom will remember what you did here.

speaker: narrator
text: You walk out of the fortress and do not look back. The road home is long, and somehow shorter than it was. Days later the hedges of Willowbrook close around you, and then you are standing at the edge of your own field.

speaker: narrator
text: Nobody has touched it since you left.

speaker: narrator
text: At the gate Grandmother is singing to herself: "Hush, little seed, the frost is going—" She sees you, and stops.

speaker: narrator
text: You kneel at the edge of the field. Your hands remember the spell you read from a stone in the glade, the one that was always yours.

speaker: narrator
text: You press your hands into the dry earth and say the smallest spell you know. Green runs out from your fingers along the rows. Leaves unfurl, the earth darkens, and the whole field breathes out at once.

speaker: narrator
text: Across the village, the chapel bell rings once, with no hand on the rope.

speaker: grandmother
text: That is the third time. The first was for her, the night she went. The second was for you, the morning you left. I do not know who this one is for.

speaker: narrator
text: You do.

speaker: narrator
text: In the hedge the little light brightens. For the last time you hear Nyx, very small:

speaker: nyx
text: Power follows purpose; purpose follows truth.

speaker: narrator
text: Grandmother opens the gate.

speaker: grandmother
text: Welcome home, Elior.

speaker: king alden
text: You named every crime and did not add one. Only someone who has paid for the truth before speaks it like that. I will remember it.

speaker: narrator
text: “Take my magic,” you say. “All of it. Close the wound with that.”

speaker: malakar
text: No. Your parents poured themselves into that wound once already. It does not get to have you too.

speaker: malakar
text: Then keep something. One thing. Anything. Do not let me take it all.

speaker: narrator
text: You press the open amulet to the wound and let go. The light, the blessing, the truth sight, every spell you carried runs out of your hands into the tear, and the tear drinks it and closes. When it is done, one small spell is still in you: grow, the one you did not inherit. You read it from a stone in a glade, and it was never theirs.

speaker: king alden
text: He will answer to me, and he will live to do it. Thank you, farmer.

speaker: lysa
text: You gave our gift back to close what he opened, and kept the one thing that was yours. That was always the best of you.

speaker: king alden
text: Go home, farmer. You have earned your field.

speaker: narrator
text: You kneel at the edge of the field. The one spell you kept stirs in your hands, the one that was never theirs, small and certain.

speaker: aren
text: We watched you give, again and again, and never ask for anything back. Today was only the last time.

speaker: narrator
text: The amulet is already open, its light filling the chamber.

speaker: narrator
text: Malakar does not answer. He is staring at the open amulet.

speaker: malakar
text: It does not hurt. For the first time in years, it does not hurt.

speaker: narrator
text: “I forgive you,” you say. The words are harder than any spell, and then they are easy. Something warm settles in your chest, like a lesson you always knew.

speaker: malakar
text: You would forgive me. They would have too.

speaker: narrator
text: You lay forgiveness on the wound. Its edges stop flickering. The days that never happened fall quiet one by one, and the tear draws closed like a healed cut. Above the circle the crystal clouds, cracks and falls away, and King Alden breathes again.

speaker: malakar
text: Thank you, Elior. I will stay here, by what I broke, and remember them properly this time.

speaker: lysa
text: You gave him back to us, our friend. We never dared hope for that.

speaker: narrator
text: The amulet is only a locket now, warm and quiet.

speaker: malakar
text: Go home, Elior. Tell Mira I am sorry, and that I remember her.

speaker: king alden
text: You saved my kingdom, and somehow him as well. Go home.

speaker: narrator
text: The field behind your home: rows of withered crops under a pale sky, the earth cracked and grey. Grandmother waits at the gate. Mira stands beside her, and Sir Cedric leans on the fence. In the hedge a small light flickers: Nyx, keeping close. The air is quiet.

speaker: grandmother
text: Your mother's. I didn't think you'd remember.

speaker: grandmother
text: You saw them. I can see it in your face.

speaker: narrator
text: “You knew,” you say. It is not a question.

speaker: grandmother
text: I knew. She made me promise, the night she went. I have not slept a whole night since.

speaker: narrator
text: You tell her what they said: that they are proud of her, that they are resting.

speaker: grandmother
text: Resting. Good. Then so can we. Go on, love. The field has waited long enough.

speaker: narrator
text: You tell her what Malakar said: that he is sorry, and that he remembers her.

speaker: mira
text: He remembers. Then I will go and see him, one day. Not yet.

speaker: narrator
text: You tell her, too, what the Sorceress asked you to carry: that she is sorry, and that Elena should hear it.

speaker: mira
text: Elena. I am going back through Greendale. I will tell her.

speaker: narrator
text: You tell him what the captain of the guard said: that he is sorry he ever doubted him.

speaker: sir cedric
text: He was the youngest on the walls that night. I never blamed him. I am glad he remembers.

speaker: sir cedric
text: And the knight in grey said his piece to my face. I have not forgiven him. Not yet.

speaker: narrator
text: He looks out over the field for a while.

speaker: sir cedric
text: Later. I have walked a long way beside you. This is a good place to stop.

speaker: narrator
text: The little light brushes your cheek, warm, and settles back into the hedge.

speaker: narrator
text: Malakar is himself again. And Elior is home.
